newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: NEW CAR SALES FALL IN Q1.
newsitem.headline: NEW CAR SALES FALL IN Q1.

text.p: New car sales in Lithuania fell to 1,396 in the first three months of 1997 from 1,598 in the same period last year, Auto Research, a local marketing research company, said on Wednesday.
Robertas Ciskevichius, a researcher with the firm, told Reuters that if the Russian-made Lada was exlcuded, the number of new cars sold in the country rose in the first three months to 739 from 680.
He said that in 1996 the total number of cars sold in Lithuania was 6,017.
"The Ladas are acquired by clients from CIS countries since it is cheaper to buy them here in Lithuaia," Cickevichius said.
He said that in the first quarter of 1997 only four percent of sold Ladas remained in the country.
Cickevichius said that during the first quarter of 1997, 657 Ladas were sold. They were followed by 133 Volkswagens, 115 Opels, 91 Skodas, 63 Fords, and 53 Hyundais.
"The new tendency during the first quarter of 1997 was the fact that the traditional leader Skoda was overtaken not only by Volkswagen but by Opel too," Cickevichius said.

He also said that the most popular model in the first quarter of the year was Skoda Felicia with 91 cars sold followed by Volkswagen Golf/Vento at 37, Volkswagen Passat with 34 sold and the Mazda 626 at 31.
